title: Categories
description: Organize the marketplace catalog into a parent/child category tree used by listings and task requests.

help.title: About Listing categories
help.overview: Listing categories are the taxonomy for the marketplace, not the product-store catalog. Listings and task requests both point at a category. Buyers browse by them; providers get matched for new task requests when they have an active listing in the same category and city.

sections.title: The tree
items: Name is what operators and the storefront show.
Parent is optional. Leave it empty for a top-level category.
Order sorts siblings (lower first). Select lists and the default list view use order, then name.
Slug is generated on create (LCAT-{name}-{random}) and is not editable afterward. It must stay unique per company.
You cannot set a category's parent to itself or to one of its descendants — that would create a cycle.
sections.body: Categories nest. A root has no parent; a child points at another category in the same company.

sections.title: How the rest of the marketplace uses them
items: Every listing must pick a category before it can be useful on the storefront.
Task requests pick a category; matching providers are those with an active listing in that category and the same city.
Demo seed data can create a broad services-style tree (design, tech, writing, and so on) for a new company.
Soft-deleted categories can be restored. Prefer fixing usage on listings over deleting a category that is still referenced.
sections.body: Categories are shared configuration under Tenancy › System settings.

sections.title: On this page
items: Create opens the category form. Edit opens an existing row.
Card and sheet views show name, slug, order, and parent.
Deleting is a soft delete and can be restored from the row actions when you have permission.
